unit.title: JavaScript: variables
unit.description: let and const, giving a name to a value, changing it, naming rules, undefined

cards.definition: Declares a variable whose value can be changed later in the program.
Declares a variable that keeps its first value: giving it a new one causes an error.
Stores the value on its right into the variable on its left; it does not compare anything.
The usual way to name variables: words joined together, each new word starting with a capital letter.
The value of a variable that has been declared but has not received any value yet.
A word that JavaScript keeps for itself (let, const, if, function) and that cannot be used to name a variable.

choices: A named box that stores a value
A line that prints some text
A file that holds the CSS
exercises.explain: A variable gives a name to a value so you can reuse it: let age = 30; stores 30 under the name age.
whyWrong: Printing is the job of console.log.
CSS files are not variables.
A mistake in the code is a bug.

exercises.explain: console.log(city) prints the value stored in city, not the word city.
whyWrong: Without quotes, city is the name of the variable: its value is printed.
console.log prints the value, without quotes.
city received a value on the first line.

exercises.explain: let allows a new value: score = 8 replaces 5. The value stored last is the one printed.
whyWrong: The second line replaces 5 with 8.
= replaces the value; it does not add.
Numbers are not glued together like text.

exercises.prompt: What happens when this code runs?
choices: An error: a const cannot get a new value
Nothing: the second line is skipped
exercises.explain: Use const for values that never change, let for values that will. Giving a const a new value throws a TypeError.
whyWrong: const means constant: the value is locked.
= replaces a value, it never adds, and here it is not even allowed.
JavaScript does not silently skip it: it stops with an error.

exercises.prompt: let total = 0; creates a variable named total that holds the number 0.
exercises.explain: let declares the variable, total is its name, and = stores the value 0 in it.

exercises.prompt: Which name follows the usual JavaScript style (camelCase)?
exercises.explain: camelCase: words joined together, each new word with a capital letter. A name cannot contain spaces or hyphens.
whyWrong: A name cannot contain a space.
A hyphen is read as a minus sign.
Special characters such as ! are not allowed in names.

exercises.explain: A variable declared without a value holds undefined until you give it one.
whyWrong: console.log prints the value, not the name.
An empty variable does not hold 0.
Declaring a variable without a value is allowed.

exercises.prompt: Build a line that creates a variable age holding 30, a value that may change later.
exercises.explain: let age = 30; uses let because the value may change. const would lock it.

exercises.prompt: This code stops with an error. Which line is wrong?
exercises.explain: price was declared with const, so it cannot receive a new value. Declare it with let if it must change.
A variable can be used in a calculation: price * 2 uses the value of price, 10.
whyWrong: Without quotes, the expression is computed.
price is 10, then it is multiplied by 2.
* multiplies; it does not glue digits together.
